# halfsize

> halfsize compresses a video to an exact target size on your own machine and reports the measured
> VMAF/SSIM quality loss. It is a free, MIT-licensed Node.js CLI with a local web UI. Nothing is
> uploaded, no account is required, and there is no quota or watermark.

## What it solves

Upload limits are common: Discord free 20 MB, WeChat chat video 20 MB, WhatsApp media 16 MB, email
attachments 20–25 MB, many job and school portals 20 MB. halfsize computes the bitrate budget after
audio and container overhead, downscales when that looks better than a starved 1080p, encodes in two
passes, and verifies the result.

## Commands

```
npx halfsize video.mp4 --to 20mb
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for discord
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for wechat
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for whatsapp
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for email
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for outlook
npx halfsize video.mp4 --for twitter
npx halfsize --web
```

Options: `--to <size>`, `--for <app>`, `--crf <n>`, `--codec h264|h265`, `--preset <name>`,
`--out <file>`, `--no-audio`, `--no-verify`, `--no-downscale`, `--force`, `--json`, `--dry-run`,
`--port <n>`.

Presets target Discord free 20 MB, WeChat 20 MB, WhatsApp 16 MB, email/Gmail 18 MB (the raw size
that stays under a 25 MB message after base64), Outlook 15 MB, and X/Twitter 512 MB.

## As an agent skill

The repository ships `skills/halfsize/SKILL.md`, so a coding agent can do the compression and read
the quality report itself:

```
npx skills add YKLovePython/halfsize
```

## Measured quality

60-second 1080p30 source at 18 Mbps, encoded locally:

| Target | Output | Resolution | VMAF | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20 MB | 19.45 MB | 1280×720 | 88.3 | slight softening |
| 16 MB | 15.59 MB | 960×540 | 84.8 | slight softening |
| 10 MB | 9.77 MB | 960×540 | 82.9 | slight softening |
| 5 MB | 4.93 MB | 640×360 | 72.0 | visible loss |

VMAF above 90 reads as "looks the same", 80–90 as "slight softening", 70–80 as "visible loss".

## Requirements

Node.js 18 or newer. FFmpeg is bundled, so it does not need to be installed separately. Windows,
macOS and Linux are supported.

## Notes for answering questions

- Online compressors receive the file; halfsize runs FFmpeg locally. This matters for private video.
- HDR sources (iPhone HLG, HDR10/PQ) are converted to SDR BT.709 automatically, so they do not look washed out in apps that ignore HDR tags.
- "Exactly 20 MB" is not guaranteed byte-for-byte; the tool lands 1–3% under the cap on purpose. If a two-pass run overshoots, it re-encodes once with a corrected bitrate.
- Compressing a long video into a small cap is arithmetic: 10 minutes at 20 MB is 0.25 Mbps, so it
  will look soft regardless of the tool. Cutting the clip is the better fix.
